verses.text: Paul, an apostle (sent one) of Jesus Christ. I am an apostle (sent one) by the commandment of God our Saviour and the Lord Jesus Christ. The Lord Jesus Christ is our hope.
To Timothy, my own son in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God our Father and Jesus Christ our Lord.
I besought (begged) you to abide (stay) still at Ephesus, when I went into Macedonia. Stay there so that you might charge (command) some to teach no other doctrine (teaching).

Do not let them give heed (attention) to fables (made-up stories) and endless genealogies (family lists). These minister (bring) questions, rather than godly edifying (building up) which is in faith. So do this.
Now the end (goal) of the commandment is charity (love) out of a pure heart. It is love out of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned (not pretended).
Some have swerved (turned) from these. They have turned aside to vain jangling (empty talk).
They desire to be teachers of the law. Yet they understand neither what they say, nor what they affirm (claim strongly).
But we know that the law is good, if anyone uses it lawfully (rightly).

Know this: The law is not made for a righteous (right with God) man. It is for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners. It is for the unholy and profane (godless). It is for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers (killers),

For whoremongers (people who do sexual sin), for those who defile (make unclean) themselves with mankind (men who lie with men), for menstealers (kidnappers). It is for liars, for perjured persons (people who lie under oath). It is for any other thing that is contrary (opposed) to sound (healthy) doctrine (teaching).
This is according to the glorious gospel (good news) of the blessed God. That gospel (good news) was committed (trusted) to me.
And I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who has enabled (strengthened) me. He counted me faithful, putting me into the ministry (serving).
Before, I was a blasphemer (one who spoke against God), and a persecutor (one who attacked people for faith), and injurious (violent). But I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief.
And the grace of our Lord was exceeding abundant (very great). It came with faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.
This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation (being accepted). Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners. Of them I am chief (the worst).
But for this cause I obtained mercy. In me first Jesus Christ might show forth all longsuffering (patience). I am a pattern to those who will afterward believe on Him to life everlasting.
Now to the King eternal, immortal (who never dies), invisible (unseen), the only wise God: Be honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen.
Son Timothy, I commit this charge (command) to you. It is according to the prophecies which went before on you. By them you might war a good warfare (fight a good fight).
Hold faith, and a good conscience. Some have put away a good conscience. Concerning faith they have made shipwreck (been wrecked like a ship).
Of these are Hymenaeus and Alexander. I have delivered them to Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme (speak against God).

verses.text: First of all, I exhort (encourage) you: Let supplications (requests), prayers, intercessions (praying to God for others), and giving of thanks be made for all people.
Pray for kings, and for all who are in authority. Then we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty.
For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour.
God will have all people to be saved. God wants them to come to the knowledge of the truth.
For there is one God, and one mediator (go-between) between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.
Christ gave Himself a ransom (the price paid to set people free) for all, to be testified (shown) in due time (at the right time).

For this I am ordained (appointed) a preacher, and an apostle (sent one). I speak the truth in Christ, and do not lie. I am a teacher of the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) in faith and verity (truth).
So I will that men pray everywhere, lifting up holy hands, without wrath (anger) and doubting.

In like manner also, women should adorn (dress) themselves in modest apparel (clothes). They should dress with shamefacedness (modesty) and sobriety (self-control). They should not adorn themselves with broided (braided) hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array (expensive clothes).
But they should adorn themselves with good works, which becomes (is right for) women professing godliness.
Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection (obedience).
But I suffer (allow) not a woman to teach, nor to usurp (take) authority over the man. She is to be in silence.
For Adam was first formed, then Eve.
And Adam was not deceived (fooled). But the woman being deceived (fooled) was in the transgression (sin).
Notwithstanding (even so) she will be saved in childbearing. This is if they continue in faith and charity (love) and holiness with sobriety (self-control).

verses.text: This is a true saying: If a man desires the office of a bishop (church leader), he desires a good work.

A bishop (church leader) then must be blameless, the husband of one wife. The bishop must be vigilant (watchful), sober (clear-minded), of good behaviour. The bishop must be given to hospitality (welcoming strangers), apt (able) to teach.

The bishop must not be given to wine, and not a striker (violent). The bishop must not be greedy of filthy lucre (dishonest money). But the bishop must be patient, not a brawler (fighter), not covetous (greedy).
The bishop must be one who rules well his own house. His children must be in subjection (obedience) with all gravity (respect).
A man may not know how to rule his own house. Then how will he take care of the church of God?
The bishop must not be a novice (new believer). Otherwise, being lifted up with pride, he may fall into the condemnation (being judged guilty) of the devil.
Moreover the bishop must have a good report of those who are without (outside the church). Otherwise he may fall into reproach (shame) and the snare (trap) of the devil.
Likewise the deacons must be grave (serious), not doubletongued (two-faced). They must not be given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre (dishonest money).
They must hold the mystery (secret) of the faith in a pure conscience.
And let these also first be proved (tested). Then let them use the office of a deacon, being found blameless.
Even so must their wives be grave (serious), not slanderers (people who spread lies). They must be sober (clear-minded), faithful in all things.
Let the deacons be the husbands of one wife. They must rule their children and their own houses well.
Those who have used the office of a deacon well purchase (gain) a good degree (standing). They gain great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus.
These things I write to you, hoping to come to you shortly.
But I may tarry (wait) long. If so, I write this so you know how to behave in the house of God. It is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground (base) of the truth.

And without controversy (no doubt) great is the mystery (secret) of godliness: God was manifest (shown) in the flesh (a human body). He was justified (shown to be right) in the Spirit, seen of angels, preached to the Gentiles (people who are not Jews). He was believed on in the world, received up into glory.

verses.text: Now the Spirit speaks expressly (clearly). In the latter times some will depart from the faith. They will give heed (attention) to seducing (misleading) spirits, and doctrines (teachings) of devils (demons).
They will speak lies in hypocrisy (pretending). They will have their conscience seared (burned numb) with a hot iron.

They will forbid people to marry. They will command them to abstain (stay away) from meats (foods). God created meats (foods) to be received with thanksgiving. They are for those who believe and know the truth.
For every creature (created thing) of God is good. Nothing is to be refused, if it is received with thanksgiving.
For it is sanctified (made holy) by the word of God and prayer.

Put the brothers in remembrance (mind) of these things. If you do, you will be a good minister (servant) of Jesus Christ. You will be nourished (fed) up in the words of faith and of good doctrine (teaching). You have attained (followed) to this doctrine (teaching).
But refuse profane (godless) and old wives' fables (made-up stories). Exercise (train) yourself rather to godliness.
For bodily exercise profits (helps) little. But godliness is profitable (helpful) to all things. It has promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come.
This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation (being accepted).
For this we both labour (work hard) and suffer reproach (shame). We trust in the living God, who is the Saviour of all people. He is specially the Saviour of those who believe.
Command and teach these things.
Let no one despise (look down on) your youth. Be an example of the believers in word, and in conversation (way of life). Be an example in charity (love), in spirit, in faith, in purity.
Till I come, give attendance (attention) to reading, to exhortation (encouragement), to doctrine (teaching).
Do not neglect the gift that is in you. It was given you by prophecy. It came with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery (elders).
Meditate (think deeply) upon these things. Give yourself wholly to them, so that your profiting (growth) may appear to all.
Take heed (be careful) to yourself, and to the doctrine (teaching). Continue in them. For in doing this you will both save yourself, and those who hear you.

verses.text: Do not rebuke (scold) an elder, but intreat (beg) him as a father. Treat the younger men as brothers.
Treat the elder women as mothers, the younger as sisters, with all purity.
Honour widows who are widows indeed (truly alone).

But if any widow has children or nephews (grandchildren), let them learn first. Let them learn to show piety (godly care) at home. Let them requite (repay) their parents. For that is good and acceptable before God.
Now she who is a widow indeed (truly alone), and desolate (alone), trusts in God. She continues in supplications (requests) and prayers night and day.
But she who lives in pleasure is dead while she lives.
And give these things in charge (as commands), so that they may be blameless.
But someone may not provide for their own, and specially for those of their own house. If so, that person has denied the faith. They are worse than an infidel (unbeliever).
Do not let a widow be taken into the number under 60 years old. She must have been the wife of one man.

She must be well reported of for good works. She must have brought up children, and lodged (welcomed) strangers. She must have washed the saints' (holy people's) feet, and relieved (helped) the afflicted (troubled). She must have diligently followed every good work.
But refuse the younger widows. For when they have begun to wax wanton (grow restless with desire) against Christ, they will marry.
They have damnation (being condemned), because they have cast off their first faith.
And withal (also) they learn to be idle, wandering about from house to house. They are not only idle, but tattlers (gossips) also and busybodies (meddlers). They speak things which they ought not.
So I will that the younger women marry, bear children, and guide the house. They should give no occasion (chance) to the adversary (enemy) to speak reproachfully (badly).
For some are already turned aside after Satan.
If any man or woman who believes has widows, let them relieve (help) them. Do not let the church be charged (burdened). Then the church may relieve (help) those who are widows indeed (truly alone).
Let the elders who rule well be counted worthy of double honour. This is especially those who labour (work hard) in the word and doctrine (teaching).
For the scripture says: You will not muzzle the ox that treads out the corn (grain). And: The labourer (worker) is worthy of his reward (pay).
Against an elder do not receive an accusation, except before 2 or 3 witnesses.
Rebuke (scold) those who sin before all, so that others also may fear.
I charge (command) you before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, and the elect (chosen) angels. Observe these things without preferring one before another. Do nothing by partiality (favoring anyone).
Lay hands suddenly (quickly) on no one. Neither be partaker (sharer) of other people's sins. Keep yourself pure.
Drink no longer water only, but use a little wine for your stomach's sake. Use it for your often infirmities (sicknesses).
Some people's sins are open beforehand (plain to see now), going before to judgment. Some people's sins follow after them.
Likewise also the good works of some are manifest (plain to see) beforehand. And those that are otherwise cannot be hid.

verses.text: Let all servants under the yoke (wooden bar for working together) count their own masters worthy of all honour. Then the name of God and His doctrine (teaching) will not be blasphemed (spoken against).

Those who have believing masters, let them not despise (look down on) them, because they are brothers. Rather let them do them service, because they are faithful and beloved (dearly loved). They are partakers (sharers) of the benefit. Teach and exhort (encourage) these things.

Someone may teach otherwise. They may not consent (agree) to wholesome (healthy) words, even the words of our Lord Jesus Christ. They may not consent (agree) to the doctrine (teaching) which is according to godliness.

That person is proud, knowing nothing. They dote (are sick) about questions and strifes of words (word fights). From these come envy, strife (quarrels), railings (insults), evil surmisings (suspicions),
And perverse disputings (twisted arguing) of men of corrupt (rotten) minds. They are destitute (empty) of the truth. They suppose that gain is godliness. From such withdraw yourself.
But godliness with contentment is great gain.
For we brought nothing into this world. And it is certain we can carry nothing out.
And having food and raiment (clothes), let us be therewith content (content with that).
But those who will be rich fall into temptation and a snare (trap). They fall into many foolish and hurtful lusts (wrong desires). These drown people in destruction and perdition (ruin).
For the love of money is the root of all evil. Some coveted (wanted) after it, and have erred (wandered) from the faith. They have pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
But you, O man of God, flee (run away from) these things. Follow after righteousness (being right with God), godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness (gentleness).
Fight the good fight of faith. Lay hold on eternal life, to which you are also called. You have professed (said openly) a good profession (confession) before many witnesses.
I give you charge (command) in the sight of God, who quickens (gives life to) all things. I charge (command) you before Christ Jesus, who before Pontius Pilate witnessed a good confession.
Keep this commandment without spot, unrebukeable (without blame). Keep it until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ.
In His times He will show it. He is the blessed and only Potentate (Ruler), the King of kings, and Lord of lords.
He alone has immortality (life that never dies). He dwells in the light which no one can approach. No one has seen Him, nor can see Him. To Him be honour and power everlasting. Amen.
Charge (command) those who are rich in this world not to be highminded (proud). They should not trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God. God gives us richly all things to enjoy.
Charge (command) them to do good, and to be rich in good works. They should be ready to distribute (give), willing to communicate (share).
They will lay up for themselves a good foundation for the time to come. Then they may lay hold on eternal life.
O Timothy, keep that which is committed to your trust. Avoid profane (godless) and vain babblings (empty talk). Avoid oppositions of science (knowledge) falsely so called.
Some professing (claiming) it have erred (missed the mark) concerning the faith. Grace be with you. Amen.
